old: Its distant root simply meant "to look" or "to watch."
In Latin, this word once meant a ghostly "appearance" or "apparition."
It shares its Latin ancestor with the English word specter.
clues: This noun, at home in both physics class and political debate, began as a Latin word for an appearance or even a ghostly apparition, something simply seen.
It names the band of colors a prism spreads light into, and, more broadly than any rainbow, a continuous range between two extremes, like opinions from left to right.
It shares a Latin ancestor with specter, and you hear it in phrases like 'across the political ___' or 'at the opposite end of the ___'.
